output.brief: The rise in falls at Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge is probably not mainly a population or medication effect. Residents' dependency, admissions and drug use barely changed, and most Q3 falls involved long-standing residents. The Hollin Street reviews stopped more medicines than they started. The more likely driver is better recording: the app went live on 1 July. Unwitnessed "found on floor" falls and no-harm falls roughly doubled, while falls causing harm rose only slightly. Q2 handover notes also show unreported falls. I can't rule out that the thinner night rota has added some real risk. There are no pre-June call-bell times, and Penmor can't produce any at all. So I can't confirm or dismiss the staff's view that bells are answered more slowly. How sure I am: moderately. I recommend keeping the pilot and not returning to four night staff now. Show falls as rates on a control chart with the change in recording marked. Start manual sampling of night call-bell response times at both homes. Set a dated review in late January using Q4 data, with the pause criteria kept in force. Don't discipline night seniors, and don't withdraw the app. Bring the board a clear interim position.
